title: Sections over a w-contractible affine are exact
statement:
Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}D$ with $D$ w-contractible be an object of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$,
and let $\mathcal R$ be a sheaf of rings on $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$. The functor
$\Gamma(U,-)\colon F\mapsto F(U)$ from abelian sheaves (or from sheaves of
$\mathcal R$-modules) to abelian groups (or $\mathcal R(U)$-modules) is exact.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and evaluate at the given object $U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact], clause 1, a kernel of abelian sheaves is the sectionwise kernel. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-limits-sectionwise], the same holds for kernels of $\mathcal R$-modules, as kernels are finite limits. Consequently, in either category, if $0\to A\xrightarrow{i}B\xrightarrow{p}C\to0$ is short exact, then $i_U$ identifies $A(U)$ with $\ker(p_U)$. Evaluation is additive: for morphisms $f,g$, $(f+g)_U=f_U+g_U$ by sectionwise addition. For modules these maps are $\mathcal R(U)$-linear, by the definition of morphism in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus evaluation is left exact in both cases.

source.place: Tag 03CO, lemma-limits-colimits-abelian-sheaves (2); Tag 03DB, lemma-limits-colimits (limits); Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian; blueprint proof opening sentence

proof.text: Let $p:F\to G$ be an epimorphism in either of the stated categories. In the module case apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], clause 1: forgetting the $\mathcal R$-action preserves cokernels, so $\operatorname{coker}(p)=0$ implies that the underlying abelian-sheaf map has zero cokernel and is an epimorphism. Its sheafification hypothesis is satisfied on the small site: the abelian sheafification functor is that of [lem-weil-pbc-sheafification-exact]. The abelian case needs no forgetting. No assertion about objectwise surjectivity has yet been used.

source.place: Tag 03DA, lemma-abelian, exactness of the forgetful functor; Tag 03CN, lemma-abelian-abelian (4), cokernels

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] to the abelian-sheaf epimorphism of step 2. For every object $V$ and $y\in G(V)$ it gives a covering $\{V_j\to V\}$ and lifts $x_j\in F(V_j)$ of $y|_{V_j}$. Forgetting the additions and scalar actions leaves exactly these sections, restrictions and equalities. Hence the underlying map of sheaves of sets is locally surjective. The reverse implication in [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheaf-sets-epi-locally-surjective] makes it an epimorphism of sheaves of sets.

source.place: Tag 03CN, lemma-abelian-abelian (5), with sites.tex Tags 00WM, definition-sheaves-injective-surjective (2), and 00WN, lemma-mono-epi-sheaves

proof.text: Apply clause 2 of [det-pe-wcb-projective] to the epimorphism of sheaves of sets obtained in step 3. Its hypotheses are exactly the given $U=\operatorname{Spec}D\in X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ and w-contractibility of $D$. It yields surjectivity of $F(U)\to G(U)$ on underlying sets, hence surjectivity of the corresponding abelian-group or $\mathcal R(U)$-linear map. Thus evaluation carries every epimorphism in either source category to a surjective homomorphism.

source.place: sentence beginning By [det-pe-wcb-projective]; det-pe-wcb-projective, statement clause 2

proof.text: Apply steps 1 and 4 to an arbitrary short exact sequence $0\to A\xrightarrow{i}B\xrightarrow{p}C\to0$. Step 1 gives injectivity of $i_U$ and $\operatorname{im}(i_U)=\ker(p_U)$, while step 4 gives surjectivity of $p_U$. Thus $0\to A(U)\to B(U)\to C(U)\to0$ is short exact. This is exactness of the additive evaluation functor, with values in abelian groups or $\mathcal R(U)$-modules respectively.

source.place: last sentence: a left exact functor preserving epimorphisms is exact, written out on an arbitrary short exact sequence
